what: Check: rustc injects `#[macro_use] extern crate std;` (core under no_std; rustc_builtin_macros/src/standard_library_imports.rs), so every #[macro_export] macro of std (format!, println!, vec!) is in the macro_use prelude. hir-def collector.rs inject_std_extern_crate defines the name but calls no import_macros_from_extern_crate, so a fixture std whose prelude does not re-export its macros gives `cannot find macro `format` in this scope` (tests::lints::bodies::types::casts::static_mut_refs::static_mut_refs_e2021/e2024 before I added `pub use crate::format;` to their std prelude). If real crates reach std's macros only through the prelude, a crate's use of a #[macro_export] macro of std that std's prelude does not re-export would fail where rustc accepts it (superset-of-rust). Import the injected crate's exported macros as MacroUse(None), as uses.rs already names.
